Hi Daniel / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the demo today — really appreciate the detailed product use cases you shared. Per our call, we want to make sure the SLA language and measurement approach match HelioMed's expectations before we send over the pilot MSA. A quick recap and a few clarifying questions so we can put a short SLO draft together: 

Key asks from HelioMed on the call:
- Interactive UI use case: clinicians will expect sub-300ms median response for autocomplete and < 800ms p95 for single-turn prompts at typical concurrency.
- Streaming transcripts for consults: first-token time is important (fast time-to-first-byte) and sustainable token throughput for long sessions.
- Burst concurrency: day-to-day concurrency ~50, but peak bursts could reach 180 concurrent streams for short windows.

Clarifying questions: 
1) For latency SLOs, do you need us to measure client-to-client (end-to-end) or server-side only (our service egress to your app)?
2) For streaming, how do you want tail measured — time-to-first-token vs. full-session tail?
3) Are network outages/proxy maintenance windows that originate inside HelioMed's VPC considered exclusions?

Next steps: if you confirm the measurement scope (Q1) and desired percentiles/time windows (Q2), I will share a one-page SLO draft and sample contract wording for review. Attached is the call recording and a placeholder SLO template we referenced.

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the quick recap, very helpful. Answers inline below: 

Q1) Measurement scope: we prefer server-side measurement (Redwood's observable metric) for the SLA so that the contract defines a clear owner for measurement and remediation. We will instrument synthetic requests from our app to confirm parity, but contractual metrics should be Redwood-measured.

Q2) Streaming tail: primary metric we care about is time-to-first-token (TTFT) for streaming start. For overall session health, we also want a 99th percentile per-token gap (to catch stalls) for sessions longer than 30s.

Q3) Exclusions: planned maintenance of HelioMed's proxies, customer-side network outages, and scheduled cloud provider maintenance windows should be excluded. Redwood-managed infra issues should not be excluded. 

Additional notes: 
- Throughput: baseline concurrency supply is 50 concurrent interactive calls, sustained for an 8-hour clinical shift. Bursts to 180 are expected for ~5–10 minute windows during handoffs.
- Reporting cadence: weekly automated SLO report PDFs and monthly incident summaries.

If you can push a draft wording that captures server-side measurement, TTFT for streaming, p95/p99 definitions, and the explicit exclusions above, we can loop in procurement/legal for a quick review.

Thanks,

Marissa / team —

Draft proposal (high level) for the SLO measurement approach — technical notes first, then contract-friendly phrasing.

Technical measurement (for Redwood telemetry):
- Interactive (single-turn) latency: measure server-side from request receive timestamp (t_recv) to final token emitted (t_last_token). Report p50 and p95 over 1-minute non-overlapping windows, then aggregate daily for SLA reporting. For clarity in contract we will define the per-request latency as (t_last_token - t_recv).
- Streaming time-to-first-token (TTFT): measure (t_first_token - t_recv). Compute rolling 1-minute windows; report p50 and p95 per-window and include a 99th percentile per-token gap computed over 30s+ sessions to detect stalls (token_gap = max inter-token delta).
- Bursts/concurrency: measure sustained concurrent active streams by sampling every 10s and report 1-minute max concurrency. For contract commitments we can define a burst-capacity guarantee of 180 concurrent streams sustained for up to a 10-minute rolling window, subject to a billing uplift or reserved capacity booking.

Contract-friendly wording (single paragraph suggestion):
"Service Latency SLOs: Redwood will measure server-side latency for requests routed to the HelioMed tenant. Latency is defined as the time elapsed from the server receive timestamp to the emission of the request's final token. For streaming workflows, time-to-first-token (TTFT) is defined as the time elapsed from server receive to the first emitted token; token-gap health is defined as the 99th percentile of inter-token intervals for sessions longer than 30 seconds. Redwood will report p50 and p95 latency and TTFT on a weekly basis and include a monthly SLO PDF for procurement. Planned customer-side network maintenance and customer-managed proxy outages are excluded from measurement. Remedies for missed SLOs will follow the schedule in Appendix A of this agreement."

Remedies (initial suggestion):
- If p95 latency exceeds target for more than two 24-hour days in a 30-day window, 5% credit of that month's invoice.
- If 99th percentile token-gap threshold is breached for more than one weekly report, 10% credit.

Notes / assumptions:
- These remedies are placeholders and will be tuned by sales/legal.
- We will instrument synthetic probes in the pilot to validate measurement parity vs. HelioMed's client-side checks.

Happy to iterate — I tried to be explicit on timestamps and windows so legal can map to observability.

Karthik
Principal SWE, Inference Runtime | karthik@redwood.com

Hi Daniel / Priya —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. Please find below the consolidated measurement approach and proposed contract language. I copied Karthik, Ben and Neha for any final technical/legal cleanups.

Consolidated measurement summary (server-side):
- Single-turn latency: per-request latency = t_last_token - t_recv. We will report p50 and p95 over non-overlapping 1-minute windows and include daily rollups for weekly/monthly reports.
- Streaming: TTFT = t_first_token - t_recv (p50, p95). Token-gap health = 99th percentile inter-token interval for sessions >30s.
- Concurrency/bursts: concurrency sampled every 10s; burst SLA covers up to 180 concurrent streams for a 10-minute rolling window (requires reserved capacity or burst add-on).
- Exclusions: planned customer-managed network/proxy maintenance and customer-side outages are excluded; Redwood-managed infra incidents are not excluded.
- Reporting cadence: weekly automated SLO PDF and monthly incident summary.

Draft contract sentence (for insertion into the MSA):
"Redwood will measure server-side latency and streaming health for the HelioMed tenant using Redwood's telemetry. Latency is defined as the interval between the server receive timestamp and the emission of the final token. For streaming workloads, Redwood will report time-to-first-token and token-gap health as defined in Appendix A. Planned customer-managed network maintenance and customer proxy outages are excluded from measurement. Remedies for missed SLOs will be as described in Appendix A."

Remediation bands (proposal, to be reviewed by legal/procurement):
- p95 exceedance: 5% credit if p95 target is missed for >48 hours in a 30-day window.
- token-gap (99p) exceedance: 10% credit if breached in two consecutive weekly reports.

Next steps
- Marissa: circulate this draft to HelioMed procurement/legal and attach the SLO appendix (attached).
- HelioMed: confirm exclusions language is acceptable to procurement.
- Redwood: Karthik to coordinate a short synthetic-probe validation session during pilot week 1.

If that reads OK, we'll route a short MSA with Appendix A (SLOs) to your procurement.

Best,
Marissa
